extracted.intended_audience: Firefox users and current Pocket customers (general web users)
extracted.subtask_description: A Mozilla blog announcement explaining the decision to phase out the Pocket apps and extensions, why the change was made, and how Firefox will continue providing content recommendations and reading-list features.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality content recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations on Firefox New Tab should be "trustworthy, engaging, and high quality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mozilla uses machine learning algorithms to scour the internet for high quality content that will appeal to Firefox’s large and diverse user base, while relying on a human editorial team to provide oversight to ensure recommendations are trustworthy, engaging, and high quality. The recommendation experience is intended to be curated and relevant to users' interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algotorial approach (algorithm + editorial oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine algorithmic machine learning with human editorial oversight to curate the best of the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ML at scale to find candidate content and employ a human editorial team to provide oversight and judgment. This hybrid approach aims to balance breadth and personalization from algorithms with trustworthiness and quality control from editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align product investments with current browsing habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel resources into projects that better match how people save and consume content on the web today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Firefox is independently funded and resource-constrained, prioritize features and projects (e.g., Tab Groups, enhanced bookmarks) that make the biggest impact on users' browsing experience rather than maintaining legacy standalone apps whose usage patterns have changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate reading-list functionality into core browser features
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide built-in ways to manage reading lists (instead of separate apps) so users can save and return to content easily within the browser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New or enhanced browser features such as Tab Groups and enhanced bookmarks are presented as alternatives to Pocket, intended to offer convenient, integrated reading-list management without requiring a separate app or extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale recommendations across geographies and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer high-quality content recommendations across multiple countries and languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mozilla has expanded content recommendations to more than a dozen countries and five languages, indicating an expectation that recommendation systems support localization and multilingual audiences when aiming for broad reach.
